policy: Original arrangements and dimensions; sources inform period massing, materials, light-court and circulation terminology. No source model, plan tracing or donor code import.

sources.title: Greenwich Village Historic District Extension II
sources.observations: The report describes the 1907 brick-and-stone H-plan at 10–12 Morton Street and its two light courts in the context of light and air requirements. The individual entry records six storeys and a mixed-use ground floor.
sources.application: H massing, open court/window relationships and restrained masonry direction only. Our three/four/five-storey residential plans are newly authored, with different unit counts, circulation and proportions.

sources.title: Dorrance Brooks Square Historic District
sources.observations: The district overview and 574 St Nicholas Avenue entry describe a 1913 H-plan apartment building with deep light courts, brick, limestone and sash windows. The overview also distinguishes a neighbouring double-H building.
sources.application: Deep open courts, masonry/sash proportions and stone-trim vocabulary. Mercer remains a single H with two linked stair cores; it is not a reconstruction of either address.

sources.title: Inside the Manhattan Building Plan Collection
sources.reviewed: Public article text and its collection overview
sources.observations: The article explains the building-plan collection and the historical development of light, ventilation, outward-facing window and fire safeguards.
sources.application: Verify actual outside-facing apartment and habitable-room windows rather than inferring exposure from an H outline. No building-plan scan is reproduced in the assets.

sources.title: Multiple Dwelling Fires, Chapter 1, section 4.2.6
sources.reviewed: Indexed primary-source excerpt, internal chapter page 21; entire 44.7 MB training manual was not downloaded
sources.observations: The section identifies concealed roof/ceiling voids, combustible construction and ineffective subdivision/firestopping as pathways for concealed spread, including an H-type example.
sources.application: Construction-specific historical notes only. These models have a closed thin roof slab and do not model a cockloft, firestop performance, fire spread or evacuation. The source does not establish that all H-plan or point-access buildings are inherently unsafe or that the type universally vanished.

sources.kind: Practitioner definition and advocacy, separate from municipal evidence
sources.title: Larch Lab Point Access Blocks policy brief
sources.reviewed: The brief endpoint returned no readable content; definition corroborated with the author's public introduction
sources.observations: The author's introduction uses point-access blocks for dwellings grouped around a stair/elevator core, as distinct from a long double-loaded corridor.
sources.application: Alder and Bellwether are single-central-stair art studies, four flats per landing. Mercer is honestly labelled as two linked point cores, two flats per core landing. No modern code, fire-safety, energy or policy performance claim is adopted.
